name: Reconcile the Account: Ladder
description: Ten frozen levels of bank reconciliation for one account: every statement line and cash-book entry matched or given a reason, every explained difference, and the adjusted balance. Levels 1-2 are one month; from level 3 a level is two to six consecutive months nobody has reconciled, and the months depend on each other: cheques, paying-ins and keyed-in payments clear in a later month, instalment plans run across months, charges are reversed and cheques returned the month after, and because the cash book was never corrected every month's balance must allow for every correction found so far and every item still outstanding at that month's end. The month balances are a quarter of the points, so one early slip carries into every later month. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
hook: Six months of bank statements nobody reconciled, each month resting on the last. How far up can it land every balance?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliation for Hollins & Webb Joinery Ltd, March 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £62,117.91.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped). The bank figure is right. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged) or "interest".
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank) or "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item and every difference. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Calder Valley Signs Ltd, May 2026 to June 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £107,630.24. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped). The bank figure is right. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), or "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.
5. The cash book has never been corrected. Each month's adjusted balance is that month's cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry found in that month AND in every earlier month. It must equal that month's statement closing balance plus the money paid in and minus the payments in the cash book (that month or before) not yet through the bank at that month's end.

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"bank": {"B101": "L102", "B102": "bank_charge", "B105": ["L106", "L107"], ...}, "ledger": {"L101": "B103", "L102": "B101", "L109": "unpresented_cheque", ...}, "differences": {"B107": {"reason": "keying_error", "amount": -270.00}}, "adjusted_balance": {"May 2026": 12345.67, "June 2026": 12345.67, ...}}
- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 43 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 5] 3 months, 98 statement lines and 96 cash-book entries, 8 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 8 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 43. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Fairhaven Events Ltd, June 2026 to August 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £120,114.60. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference, which can run over several months), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement, in the same month or the next: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid, in the same month or later; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.
5. The cash book has never been corrected. Each month's adjusted balance is that month's cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry found in that month AND in every earlier month. It must equal that month's statement closing balance plus the money paid in and minus the payments in the cash book (that month or before) not yet through the bank at that month's end, counting a payment made in instalments by the part not yet through.

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"bank": {"B101": "L102", "B102": "bank_charge", "B105": ["L106", "L107"], ...}, "ledger": {"L101": "B103", "L102": "B101", "L109": "unpresented_cheque", ...}, "differences": {"B107": {"reason": "keying_error", "amount": -270.00}}, "adjusted_balance": {"June 2026": 12345.67, "July 2026": 12345.67, ...}}
- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 46 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 6] 3 months, 109 statement lines and 109 cash-book entries, 9 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 8 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 46. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Marsh Lane Motors Ltd, May 2026 to August 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £155,684.36. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference, which can run over several months), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement, in the same month or the next: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid, in the same month or later; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"bank": {"B101": "L102", "B102": "bank_charge", "B105": ["L106", "L107"], ...}, "ledger": {"L101": "B103", "L102": "B101", "L109": "unpresented_cheque", ...}, "differences": {"B107": {"reason": "keying_error", "amount": -270.00}}, "adjusted_balance": {"May 2026": 12345.67, "June 2026": 12345.67, ...}}
- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 48 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 7] 4 months, 148 statement lines and 144 cash-book entries, 14 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 11 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 48. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Hollins & Webb Joinery Ltd, June 2026 to September 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £172,697.72. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference, which can run over several months), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement, in the same month or the next: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid, in the same month or later; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.
5. The cash book has never been corrected. Each month's adjusted balance is that month's cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry found in that month AND in every earlier month. It must equal that month's statement closing balance plus the money paid in and minus the payments in the cash book (that month or before) not yet through the bank at that month's end, counting a payment made in instalments by the part not yet through.

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"bank": {"B101": "L102", "B102": "bank_charge", "B105": ["L106", "L107"], ...}, "ledger": {"L101": "B103", "L102": "B101", "L109": "unpresented_cheque", ...}, "differences": {"B107": {"reason": "keying_error", "amount": -270.00}}, "adjusted_balance": {"June 2026": 12345.67, "July 2026": 12345.67, ...}}
- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 50 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 8] 4 months, 162 statement lines and 162 cash-book entries, 13 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 11 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 50. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Calder Valley Signs Ltd, January 2026 to May 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £196,033.86. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference, which can run over several months), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement, in the same month or the next: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid, in the same month or later; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.
5. The cash book has never been corrected. Each month's adjusted balance is that month's cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry found in that month AND in every earlier month. It must equal that month's statement closing balance plus the money paid in and minus the payments in the cash book (that month or before) not yet through the bank at that month's end, counting a payment made in instalments by the part not yet through.

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"bank": {"B101": "L102", "B102": "bank_charge", "B105": ["L106", "L107"], ...}, "ledger": {"L101": "B103", "L102": "B101", "L109": "unpresented_cheque", ...}, "differences": {"B107": {"reason": "keying_error", "amount": -270.00}}, "adjusted_balance": {"January 2026": 12345.67, "February 2026": 12345.67, ...}}
- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 52 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 9] 5 months, 206 statement lines and 200 cash-book entries, 22 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 14 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 52. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the bank reconciliations for Calder Valley Signs Ltd, January 2026 to June 2026? The account was fully reconciled at the end of the month before, so the statement and the cash book both opened at £217,222.87. Our bookkeeper has been off, so nothing has been reconciled or corrected since: every month is below.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date (a cheque can take longer: any time after its cash-book date, in a later month too), and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference, which can run over several months), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly. Statement lines and cash-book entries are numbered through the months (B1.. and L1.. in the first month, B2.. and L2.. in the second, ...). An entry is matched with the line that clears it in whichever month that is.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement, in the same month or the next: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid, in the same month or later; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched). Use these reasons only for entries still not through the bank at the end of the last month.
5. The cash book has never been corrected. Each month's adjusted balance is that month's cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry found in that month AND in every earlier month. It must equal that month's statement closing balance plus the money paid in and minus the payments in the cash book (that month or before) not yet through the bank at that month's end, counting a payment made in instalments by the part not yet through.

- bank: every statement line, with the cash-book entry it matches (a list for a split or a BACS run) or its reason from rule 3.
- ledger: every cash-book entry, with the bank line it matches (a list for a split) or its reason from rule 4.
- differences: one entry per matched bank line whose amount differs from the cash book (rule 2); leave it empty ({}) if there are none.
- adjusted_balance: the adjusted balance at the end of each month, keyed by the month as written above (rule 5), in pounds to the penny.
Marking: each bank line, each cash-book entry, each difference's reason and amount and each adjusted balance is a field. Routine fields (a straightforward match) are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (an entry cleared in another month, a split, a duplicate, a reversal, a keying or FX difference, a timing item) are worth 3, and each adjusted balance is worth 55 (the balances together are about a quarter of the points). Every difference you list that is not one costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter, and amounts may have a £ sign. Give one value per field: a field with two answers is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 10] 6 months, 263 statement lines and 255 cash-book entries, 32 entries cleared in a later month. Rules in play: the basics (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees, interest) + 10 families (keying, dd, duplicates, carry, splits, reversal, returned, batch, fx, instalments); 17 explained differences. Key = the generator's own transaction list (Rec of verification/realworld-work/bankrec.py over several months); second derivations: every month's adjusted balance computed from the cash-book side and from the bank side agrees, and every one-to-one match is re-derived from the printed fields alone and is the only candidate. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each month's balance 55. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
